source: Wang, Li, Qiao, ... Luo (2025/2026) Increasing Computation Resolves Conflicts in Vision Language Models (Machine psychophysics: cognitive control in VLMs)
finding: 47 VLMs on 4,410 Stroop, Flanker and object-level conflict tasks. Every model shows a congruency effect. Larger models resolve conflict better.
numbers: Non-squared tasks: mean accuracy 0.852 congruent vs 0.567 incongruent (diff 0.285, t=13.981, p=3.6e-25). Squared (high-conflict) tasks: 0.634 vs 0.297 (diff 0.337).
limits: Parameter count is used as a proxy for processing time. This is a cross-sectional analogy, not a within-model time manipulation. Images plus text, not pure text.
agent_relevance: Executive-control-like interference is the default state of a model. A scaffold step that resolves conflict should expect to pay for it.

source: Wang, Li, Qiao, ... Luo (2025/2026) Increasing Computation Resolves Conflicts in Vision Language Models (Machine psychophysics: cognitive control in VLMs)
finding: Per-paradigm table: classic Stroop and Flanker show small gaps in the easy design, but object-level conflicts (text overlaid on an object) show large gaps.
numbers: Easy design, cong vs incong: Stroop-color 0.968 vs 0.931 (p=0.153); Flanker-letter 0.873 vs 0.860 (ns); Flanker-number 0.859 vs 0.824 (p=0.0147); Word Overlay 0.977 vs 0.813 (p=5e-13); Sentence Overlay 0.977 vs 0.825. Squared design: Stroop 0.591 vs 0.366; Word Overlay 0.719 vs 0.265 (diff 0.454).
limits: Classic Stroop effect is near ceiling for strong models, so the diagnostic power sits in harder variants.
agent_relevance: Text in the input that competes with the task target is the strongest distractor. Expect this for instructions embedded in tool output.

source: Wang, Li, Qiao, ... Luo (2025/2026) Increasing Computation Resolves Conflicts in Vision Language Models (Machine psychophysics: cognitive control in VLMs)
finding: Larger models drop BELOW chance on incongruent high-conflict trials while small models sit at chance on both. The authors map this to the human short-processing-time dip.
numbers: Small models: chance on congruent and incongruent squared trials. Large models: above chance congruent, below chance incongruent. Modality preference: in Stroop-object, 74.5% of models prefer OCR targets (mean diff 0.100, SD 0.255, r=0.611); in Stroop 37 of 43 models (86.0%) balanced (|diff|<=0.05), mean diff 0.084.
limits: Below-chance incongruent accuracy means the model actively follows the distractor. The human parallel is argued, not proven.
agent_relevance: Reading beats perceiving. A scaffold should present the task-relevant channel in a form that text cannot override.

source: Hu (2025) Conflict Adaptation in Vision-Language Models
finding: Sequential Stroop with two words per image. 12 of 13 VLMs do better on an incongruent trial after an incongruent trial (II) than after a congruent one (CI), the human conflict-adaptation signature.
numbers: 13 open VLMs (Gemma, InternVL, Molmo, Qwen). 30 CC, 120 CI, 120 IC, 360 II sequences per layout. Only exception Qwen2.5-VL-72B, which was 100% in all conditions (ceiling, author's guess). Layout (left-right vs top-down) did not matter.
limits: Measured as log probability of the correct second token. Could be a within-trial effect of the first word, not true carry-over of control. No humans run as comparison.
agent_relevance: In-context history can raise or lower later interference. A sequence of hard items may prime better control. Test this order effect in our loop.

source: Hu (2025) Conflict Adaptation in Vision-Language Models
finding: Sparse transcoder analysis of InternVL 3.5 4B finds text and colour supernodes, and a conflict-modulated supernode in layers 24-25. Ablating it raises Stroop errors but barely touches congruent trials.
numbers: Text supernode layers 3-15 and 19-33; colour supernode layers 8-11 and 19-33. Text supernode larger in early layers, colour larger in late layers. Conflict features are dense and not interpretable.
limits: One 4B model only. Transcoders came from the base language model, not the VLM. Authors flag this.
agent_relevance: A small, dense, conflict-gated component exists, like an executive-control network invoked only when needed.

source: Teker, Xiao, Akata, Wu (2026) Feature Competition and Its Representational Origins in Vision-Language Models: Evidence from the Stroop Paradigm
finding: CLIP and SigLIP-2 read the word far better than they report ink colour. Six generative VLMs mostly answer with the written word.
numbers: 100 images (10 congruent, 90 incongruent). CLIP word-prompt 97.8% vs ink-prompt about 20%. SigLIP-2 100% vs 5-6%. CLIP word accuracy 85-97% across font/contrast changes, ink 20-30%. Nonword stimuli: about 78% ink-aligned. Larger corpus 23,338 images: word 99.5%, ink 15.9%. Kosmos-2 never reported ink. LLaVA ink-aligned in only 54.4% of incongruent trials.
limits: Small hand-made benchmark. Contrastive scores are not the same as chat answers. Preprint.
agent_relevance: Without any control step, the dominant channel wins. Automaticity (reading) is stronger than the task target.

source: Teker, Xiao, Akata, Wu (2026) Feature Competition and Its Representational Origins in Vision-Language Models: Evidence from the Stroop Paradigm
finding: Prompt wording changes Stroop interference a lot. Telling the model to ignore the word did worse than a short prompt that never mentions the word.
numbers: Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct, incongruent ink accuracy: long 'ignore the written word' prompt 31.1%; short 'What is the ink color...' prompt 60.0%. Across nine more prompt variants ink accuracy ranged 24% to 97%.
limits: Single model, 45 incongruent items per cell. Mechanism (priming) is the authors' guess.
agent_relevance: Naming the distractor in an inhibit instruction may prime it. Prefer reframing the task over a 'do not attend to X' rule. Relevant to guardrail wording.

source: Teker, Xiao, Akata, Wu (2026) Feature Competition and Its Representational Origins in Vision-Language Models: Evidence from the Stroop Paradigm
finding: Word identity is encoded along stronger, more separable directions than ink colour in CLIP embeddings. Steering along word directions works; colour directions do not.
numbers: RSA: adding word shape on top of colour makes image embeddings far more dissimilar than adding colour on top of words. Steering along word-related directions shifts behaviour reliably; colour-direction steering is weaker and entangled.
limits: CLIP only for the mechanistic part.
agent_relevance: Saliency asymmetry predicts which cue wins. A scaffold can raise the salience of the target cue instead of fighting the distractor.

source: Hu, Angstadt, Storks, ... Sripada (2026) Conflict and Congruency Effects in Large Language Models: In-Weight and In-Context Competition in a Verbal Conflict Task
finding: Text-only conflict task. A stem gives a default same-colour completion; an in-context rule either agrees (congruent) or conflicts (incongruent). Six of seven models show strong congruency effects.
numbers: Gemma-2-2B, 40 prompts per condition. Default same-colour next-token probability 0.5074 vs 0.0822 for the runner-up. Correct-response probability gap: congruent 0.9644 vs incongruent 0.5676, diff 0.3968, 95% CI [0.3529, 0.4407], t(39)=18.28. Accuracy 100% in both. Pythia 410M to 12B also tested.
limits: Small models and a synthetic crayon prompt. Accuracy hides the effect; only probabilities show it.
agent_relevance: A text-only Stroop analogue exists for LLM scaffolds. Accuracy can be perfect while the margin is weak, so measure margins.

source: Hu, Angstadt, Storks, ... Sripada (2026) Conflict and Congruency Effects in Large Language Models: In-Weight and In-Context Competition in a Verbal Conflict Task
finding: Two attention pathways: short-range attention to a surface colour cue (congruent) and long-range attention to the rule prefix (incongruent). Ablating attention to the satisfied consequent hurts incongruent trials only.
numbers: Ablation changed congruent probability by 0.0962 but incongruent by 0.8829 (difference 0.7864, t=43.15).
limits: Mechanism shown in one 2B model with a matching story in Pythia.
agent_relevance: Control means keeping a long-range pointer to the rule. A scaffold should restate the rule near the point of decision.

source: Hu, Angstadt, Storks, ... Sripada (2026) Conflict and Congruency Effects in Large Language Models: In-Weight and In-Context Competition in a Verbal Conflict Task
finding: Making the default stronger by fine-tuning hurts incongruent and helps congruent performance. Bigger rule sets hurt only incongruent trials.
numbers: Congruent margin rose from 0.9644 to 0.9846 (p=0.001) while incongruent fell. Same direction in all six Pythia models (e.g. 410M p<5.7e-8). Larger rule set selectively reduced incongruent performance.
limits: A mechanistic account of competition, not a replication of the ANT.
agent_relevance: Long rule lists weaken override of habits. Keep active rules few (supports our guardrail count limits).

source: Zhao, Huang, Ge, Wu (2026) What Color Is the Text? A Benchmark for Hallucination Induced by Image-Embedded Prompt (Embedded Stroop, WCIT)
finding: Embedded Stroop: the query is rendered inside the image. 16 proprietary and open MLLMs answer the embedded word instead of the true text colour.
numbers: Pooled over models: exact colour accuracy 6.3% (59 colours); coarse accuracy 38.4% (11 families); Stroop Hallucination Rate 21.6%. Conditional SHR on colours the model can name 51.9%, 95% CI [35.4, 66.8]. Table 1 SHR (hard template): GPT-4o 47.0, GPT-5.2 25.0, Gemini-2.5-Flash 19.0, Gemini-3-Flash 14.0, Qwen3-VL-Plus 53.0; standard Stroop SHR 5.5-34.5 per model. 56 of 64 conditions significant after FDR.
limits: Single benchmark; the 59-colour task is hard so accuracy is low for all.
agent_relevance: Even frontier models are captured by text embedded in the input. Embedded instruction injection is the agent version.

source: Zhao et al. (2026) WCIT
finding: Masking or flipping the embedded text lowers hallucination. An adversarial-aware prompt cuts SHR by up to 91%.
numbers: Masking 25% of the text significantly lowers SHR; a residual SHR remains in many cases. Prompt reduction up to 91% (best case).
limits: Best-case figure; average reduction was not extracted from the text read.
agent_relevance: A warning prompt (an alerting cue) plus removing the distractor works. Alerting plus filtering is the machine version.

source: Wang (2026) Persistent Priors, Preserved Targets: A Stroop-Style Paradigm for Lexical Override
finding: Local redefinition ('doctor means forest') leaves interference from the familiar associate (hospital). All 11 model settings show positive interference.
numbers: 11 open-weight settings (Qwen, Gemma, OLMo, Mistral). OLS slope of interference on prior preference 0.086 (p<1e-9). Antonym family slope null (+0.026, p=0.235); other families +0.150 to +0.202. Patching neutral-control activations at defined word, definition target and query restores margin: recovery 0.92-1.06 in five 1B-2B models.
limits: Small open models; interference is invisible to plain accuracy.
agent_relevance: Redefinitions in a scaffold (renaming states or operators) leak old meaning. Use fresh labels, not familiar words.

source: Shi, Chen, Misra, ..., Zhou (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context (GSM-IC)
finding: One irrelevant sentence added to grade-school maths drops accuracy sharply. A flanker-like distractor effect in text.
numbers: code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003; fewer than 30% of base problems are solved consistently after adding distractors (macro accuracy). Role-overlap distractors drop text-davinci-003 macro accuracy to 0 for problems with more than 2 steps.
limits: 2022-era GPT-3.5 models, not current ones.
agent_relevance: Irrelevant context is a standard failure. Supports filtering the context before reasoning.

source: Shi et al. (2023) GSM-IC
finding: Mitigations: self-consistency, exemplars that include distractors, and an instruction to ignore irrelevant information. Self-consistency helps most.
numbers: Self-consistency (20 samples) raised overall micro accuracy by more than 11 points; 0-COT gain 35.5 points. Correct answer present in 20 samples for 99.7% of problems. Best macro accuracy with SC still only 45%. 'Feel free to ignore' instruction raised the first accuracy column of Table 3 (COT 73.5 to 79.0, LTM 74.9 to 80.1) with no loss on GSM8K (59.3 to 60.3).
limits: Contrasts with the S2A finding below, where an ignore-instruction gave no consistent gain.
agent_relevance: Sampling plus voting, and distractor exemplars, are cheap controls. Matches our diversity operators.

source: Weston, Sukhbaatar (2023) System 2 Attention (is something you might need too)
finding: S2A: the model first rewrites the context to keep only relevant parts, then answers from the rewrite. This is an executive-control step implemented in an LLM loop.
numbers: LLaMA-2-70B-chat. Opinion-laden QA: factuality 62.8% baseline to 80.3% S2A (oracle 82.0%). Longform objectivity 2.23 baseline vs 3.82 S2A (oracle 3.0, scale 0-5). GSM-IC: S2A gains about 12 points (random distractors) and 10 (in-topic).
limits: One model family; GPT-4 as grader; 200 prompts for QA. Costs two calls.
agent_relevance: Direct template for a filter-then-reason step in our schema. Costs one extra call.

source: Weston, Sukhbaatar (2023) System 2 Attention
finding: Ablations: adding an instruction to ignore irrelevant text gave no consistent gain; a variant that keeps the original context beside the rewrite is worse and still sycophantic.
numbers: Instructed prompting did not help consistently on GSM-IC. Keeping original context with the relevant part: 74.5% vs S2A 80.3% factuality. Another variant 62.8% to 71.7% but sycophancy remained.
limits: Ablations on one model.
agent_relevance: Remove the distractor, do not just tell the model to ignore it. Consistent with the Stroop VLM prompt finding.

source: Liu, Lin, Hewitt, ..., Liang (2023) Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
finding: Position of the relevant passage gives a U-shaped accuracy curve. Models use the start and end of the context best. A spatial-orienting analogue.
numbers: GPT-3.5-Turbo multi-document QA: closed-book 56.1%, oracle 88.3%; mid-position accuracy can fall more than 20% and in 20- and 30-document settings falls below closed-book. Claude-1.3 closed-book 48.3%, oracle 76.1%. Key-value retrieval worst case 45.6% without query-aware contextualization, perfect with it for 300 pairs.
limits: 2023 models; later long-context models may differ.
agent_relevance: Place the key rule at the start or end of the prompt, and repeat the query at both ends.

source: Han, Song, Yu, You (2024) In-Context Learning May Not Elicit Trustworthy Reasoning: A-Not-B Errors in Pretrained Language Models
finding: Few-shot examples that always answer 'A', then a switched correct answer: a response-inhibition test. Models keep answering A.
numbers: Drops as large as 83.3% (Qwen1.5-7b, 25 shots; 36% to 6% in the table cell). Llama3-70b fell 32.6% at 25 shots on the same task. Larger models average drop 8.7% at 25 shots vs 20.8% for smaller. Llama2-70b was worse than Llama3-8b, so pretraining data matters.
limits: Multiple choice with trivial context changes. Four reasoning tasks only. No mitigation tested.
agent_relevance: Repeated same-answer exemplars create prepotent responses. Vary exemplar answers.

source: He, Feng (2026) When to Think Deeply: Inhibitory Deliberation for LLM Reasoning (IDPR)
finding: An LLM-loop method that borrows executive control: draft a fast answer, then an inhibition controller decides whether to suppress it for slow reasoning. Uses confidence, logit margin, parseability and generation cost of the fast answer.
numbers: 5,000-example maths test: slow reasoning on 8.20% of items lifts accuracy from 47.90% to 48.92%. Random routing at the same budget 46.76%; best confidence baseline 48.22%.
limits: Gain is only about 1 point. Cites Botvinick 2001 and Shenhav 2013, not the ANT. Uses a trained controller.
agent_relevance: A budgeted control step conditioned on the fast answer beats random routing. Matches our gate between fast and slow states.

source: Bandara et al. (2026) Think Before You Act - A Neurocognitive Governance Model for Autonomous AI Agents
finding: Position paper for an agent governance loop modelled on a System 2 deliberate pause. Only the framing sections were read.
numbers: No benchmark numbers found in the sections read.
limits: Skimmed; claims are conceptual. Does not cite the ANT.
agent_relevance: The 'pause before action' idea is the alerting analogue.

source: Binz, Schulz (2023) Using cognitive psychology to understand GPT-3 (PNAS)
finding: GPT-3 given classic tasks: good on standard vignettes but fragile under small changes. A method for putting LLMs through human paradigms.
numbers: 12 vignettes: all answered correctly or in a human-like way, 6 of 12 correct. Adversarial changes broke it, e.g. cab problem answered '20%'. All three CRT items answered with the intuitive wrong answer.
limits: No attention-network paradigm tested; training-set contamination possible.
agent_relevance: Warn that famous paradigms may be memorised. Use novel variants.

source: Ortu, Jin, Doimo, Cazzaniga (2025/2026) When Seeing Overrides Knowing: Disentangling Knowledge Conflicts in Vision-Language Models
finding: Counterfactual images conflict with model knowledge. A small set of attention heads mediates the conflict, and steering them shifts the answer.
numbers: Factual accuracy drops to 27% (LLaVA-NeXT) and 24% (Gemma3) once the image conflicts with memory. Raising attention from selected heads in LLaVA-NeXT lifts factual accuracy to 74%.
limits: Only two VLMs; counterfactual commonsense, not a Stroop task.
agent_relevance: Conflict between context and memory is handled by few heads. A direct causal route to executive-control-like intervention.

source: Fan, McCandliss, Sommer, Raz, Posner (2002) Testing the efficiency and independence of attentional networks
finding: Original ANT paper. NOT opened this session. No language-model study of the ANT itself was found in my arXiv searches (queries for attention network test returned none).
numbers: Not extracted.
limits: Absence claim limited to arXiv search of a few queries. WebSearch, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex were rate limited.
agent_relevance: The ANT itself looks untested on LLMs. A gap that background-only work can note.

source: Cohen, Dunbar, McClelland (1990) On the control of automatic processes: a PDP account of the Stroop effect
finding: Older computational system: a connectionist model where attention modulates pathways and reading is stronger because of more training. Not opened.
numbers: Not extracted.
limits: Not opened. Cited from memory only.
agent_relevance: Teker 2026 and Hu 2025 echo the same logic in transformers: practice asymmetry gives automaticity.

source: Botvinick, Braver, Barch, Carter, Cohen (2001) Conflict monitoring and cognitive control
finding: Conflict-monitoring model: a monitor detects response conflict and raises control, giving conflict adaptation. Cited by the IDPR and Hu papers. Not opened.
numbers: Not extracted.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Basis for the conflict-adaptation test in c04 and the inhibition controller in c21.
